source: Kassner, Tafjord, Schutze, Clark (2021) BeliefBank: Adding Memory to a Pre-Trained Language Model for a Systematic Notion of Belief
finding: A coherence-style layer on top of a fixed language model: store its yes/no answers, add pairwise constraints (implication, mutual exclusion), and run a weighted MaxSAT solver that flips beliefs that clash with the most others. This is the same idea as ECHO (links that excite or inhibit, pick the best-satisfying assignment), done by code, not by the model.
numbers: Model: Macaw (T5, 400k QA pairs). Raw model about 72% F1 and about 72-73% consistency. Constraint solver alone: about 96% consistency and accuracy about +17 points over raw. Solver plus relevant feedback: F1 86.6 and consistency 97.0 after batch 10 (Table 1 and appendix B). Weights tuned on 1,072 calibration facts about 7 entities.
quote: improving consistency in this way improves accuracy
limits: Toy domain: simple facts (is a poodle a dog) with hand-made, gold constraints. Constraint weights were tuned on a dev set. Authors show the solver can flip a correct belief when many weak constraints add up (rat flipped to cat).
agent_relevance: Direct support for 'selection by code': let the program, not the model, decide which of several conflicting claims to keep, using a weighted constraint graph. Needs trustworthy constraints.

source: Kassner et al. (2021) BeliefBank, ablation of feedback and ordering
finding: Feeding the model its own earlier relevant beliefs as context (chosen using the constraint graph) raises consistency but not as much as the solver. Doing it incrementally beats doing it once with all raw answers.
numbers: Relevant feedback consistency about 81% at batch 10 vs about 72% for on-topic random feedback and raw. Non-incremental 'omniscient' feedback: accuracy 74.5%, lower than incremental approaches.
limits: Same toy setting. Feedback can amplify wrong beliefs if the fed-back beliefs are wrong (authors say so).
agent_relevance: Order matters: correct beliefs early, then reuse them. A scaffold should settle checked facts first and carry them forward, not re-ask everything from raw guesses.

source: Jung, Qin, Welleck, Brahman, Bhagavatula, Le Bras, Choi (2022) Maieutic Prompting: Logically Consistent Reasoning with Recursive Explanations
finding: Ask GPT-3 for an explanation tree (X is true because ..., and X is false because ...), score pairwise logical relations with an NLI model, then use weighted MaxSAT to choose truth values. This is a coherence network over the model's own claims, solved by code.
numbers: Com2Sense dev accuracy 72.5 vs Self-Consistency 61.4 (N=20 samples) and GKP 61.8. Up to 20% better than other prompting methods on Com2Sense, CSQA 2.0, CREAK. Max tree 18 nodes.
quote: performs up to 20% better than other prompting methods, and performs on par or even better than supervised models
limits: True/false statements only. Accuracy saturates with tree size because of topic drift. The model's explanations can be factual even for wrong answers, so the graph still depends on weak inputs.
agent_relevance: Strong case that a constraint solver beats plain majority voting over samples (consistent with guardrail G4 that samples are not independent). Cost: many model calls per question.

source: Jung et al. (2022) Maieutic Prompting, ablations
finding: Which parts of the coherence network matter: the NLI relation checker and abductive generation both help.
numbers: Remove the NLI verifier and use likelihood-based consistency: accuracy drops about 7%. Remove abductive generation (no answer label given): drops about 4%. Com2Sense dev ablation.
limits: Single dataset ablation (Com2Sense dev). GPT-3 only.
agent_relevance: The quality of the link weights (here from NLI) is the main lever. Garbage links give garbage coherence.

source: Mitchell, Noh, Li, Armstrong, Agarwal, Liu, Finn, Manning (2022) ConCoRD: Enhancing Self-Consistency and Performance of Pre-Trained Language Models through Natural Language Inference
finding: Build a factor graph from the model's candidate answers plus NLI-detected entail/contradict links, then solve with weighted MaxSAT. No fine-tuning. Gains are larger on consistency tasks and modest on open QA.
numbers: BeliefBank F1 Macaw-Large 0.831 to 0.914, Macaw-3B 0.855 to 0.931; consistency 0.835 to 0.920 and 0.871 to 0.947. ConVQA accuracy LXMERT 0.656 to 0.706 (+5 points), ViLT 0.784 to 0.804. Natural Questions F1 T5-Sm 0.207 to 0.225, T5-Lg 0.314 to 0.328, T5-3B 0.332 to 0.351. With gold constraints (oracle) gains are larger (e.g. NQ T5-3B 0.423).
limits: Gap to oracle shows the NLI link detector is the bottleneck. Best NLI model differs by task (Albert-XXL best on NQ, RoBERTa-Large better on BeliefBank and ConVQA). Hyperparameters tuned per task.
agent_relevance: Expect small gains (1-2 points) on open-ended tasks, bigger on tasks with many cross-checkable claims. Link detection quality caps the benefit.

source: Mitchell et al. (2022) ConCoRD, relation-type ablation and injection
finding: Using both entail and contradict links is as good or better than either alone; the two carry partly redundant information. Adding gold context as a node edits model behaviour without retraining.
numbers: Table 5: BeliefBank Macaw-Large F1 0.914 (both) vs 0.892 (contradiction only) vs 0.827 (entailment only). ConVQA LXMERT 0.706 vs 0.691 vs 0.700. Table 4: injecting gold NQ context raised F1 over base for all 3 sizes.
limits: Relation model robust to settings but best NLI model varies.
agent_relevance: Include both support and conflict edges in any coherence check; conflict-only or support-only graphs lose accuracy on some tasks.

source: Tafjord, Dalvi Mishra, Clark (2022) Entailer: Answering Questions with Faithful and Truthful Chains of Reasoning
finding: Backward-chain from an answer to premises, then keep only proofs whose premises the model itself believes (self-query). A belief-consistency filter on reasoning chains, without losing accuracy.
numbers: OBQA 75.2 and QuaRTz 75.4 for proof-based answers vs 75.2 and 74.1 direct (no significant difference). Annotators: over 70% of Entailer proofs clearly follow vs 34% for Macaw explanations. Cost: 80 s per question (depth 1) or 360 s (depth 3, k=6) on a 48GB GPU.
quote: no significant accuracy penalty for proof-based answers
limits: Faithfulness is lost when proof score and direct score are combined (answer chosen not from best proof for 16.8% of OBQA, 14.2% QuaRTz). Failure causes: 33% wrong beliefs, 10% basic reasoning errors, 9% unsound abduction (A because A implies B and B). Small science QA datasets.
agent_relevance: Coherence filtering buys explainability, not accuracy. If we want accuracy gains we need the external constraint solver (b01, b03), not just belief-checked chains.

source: Dalal, Valentino, Freitas, Buitelaar (2024/2025) Inference to the Best Explanation in Large Language Models (IBE-Eval)
finding: Score competing LLM explanations by features taken from explanation-coherence theory: logical consistency, parsimony (proof depth, concept drift), coherence, and hedging. Pick the explanation with the best linear score.
numbers: Up to 77% accuracy at picking the explanation tied to the correct answer (27 points above random, about 17 above a GPT-3.5-as-judge baseline) on COPA and E-CARE (500 sampled E-CARE test items). Human check: 100 explanation pairs, humans picked the correct-answer explanation 96% (COPA) and 91% (E-CARE); kappa .68. Spearman with human preference 0.64 (p<.01) for IBE-Eval vs 0.31 (not significant) for GPT-3.5 judge.
limits: Causal QA with two options, GPT-3.5 and LLaMA 2 only. Linguistic uncertainty was the strongest single predictor. Two raters, both authors.
agent_relevance: Explanation-quality features computed by code can beat an LLM judge. Hedging and extra concepts are cheap, countable signals of a weak explanation.

source: Dalal et al. (2024/2025) IBE-Eval, consistency finding
finding: LLMs are strong rationalizers: they write logically consistent explanations at equal rates for correct and incorrect options. So logical consistency alone does not separate true from false; parsimony and hedging do.
numbers: Fig. 3: consistency equal for explanations of correct and wrong options. Negative correlations between proof depth, concept drift and accuracy. About 2% of cases were self-evident explanations.
limits: Only two models and two datasets.
agent_relevance: Same trap as in human coherence-shift: a story can be fully coherent and false. Coherence is a ranking signal only if the inputs (evidence) are anchored to checks.

source: Freedman, Dejl, Gorur, Yin, Rago, Toni (2025) Argumentative Large Language Models for Explainable and Contestable Claim Verification (AAAI 2025)
finding: LLM writes pro and con arguments and base scores; a formal gradual semantics (DF-QuAD, also a Quadratic Energy ablation) computes the final claim strength. A weighted argument network, solved by code, much like ECHO.
numbers: Accuracy comparable to chain-of-thought, not better. Best were Direct Questioning, CoT and ArgLLM with estimated base score. On MedClaim with GPT-4o, Direct and CoT were best, then Est. Base Arg (depth 1). Quadratic Energy results closely matched DF-QuAD. Datasets: TruthfulClaim, StrategyClaim, MedClaim (200 data points in the Mixtral prompt tests).
limits: Authors say zero-shot argument generation and scoring is limited even for strong models. Gains are in contestability, not accuracy.
agent_relevance: A network that settles a verdict by code gives an audit trail and a place to contest, but do not expect an accuracy gain over CoT. Semantics choice mattered little.

source: Simon (2004) A Third View of the Black Box: Cognitive Coherence in Legal Decision Making, Univ. Chicago Law Review 71(2):511
finding: Abstract only (full PDF blocked). Argues legal decisions fit neither the Rationalist nor the Critical model. Reasoning runs both ways: facts and premises shape the verdict, and the leaning verdict reshapes how facts are seen, inflating support for the favoured side. Applies this to four trial stages and proposes procedures to reduce error.
numbers: No numbers in the abstract.
limits: Only the abstract was read this session. The experimental figures cited by this paper are not verified here.
agent_relevance: The human pattern the coherence models are built to explain: bidirectional distortion of evidence. For the agent, this is the failure to guard against, not copy.

source: Thagard (1989) Explanatory coherence, Behavioral and Brain Sciences 12(3):435-467
finding: From memory, not opened: ECHO is a connectionist network. Propositions are units; explanation, contradiction and analogy give excitatory or inhibitory links; seven principles fix them; activation is run until it settles; accepted propositions are those with positive activation. Applied to historical science cases (oxygen vs phlogiston, Copernicus, Darwin) and a legal case.
numbers: Not verified this session. Exact link weights and the list of simulated cases need checking against the paper.
limits: Search snippet only in the series row. Later critics say the weights and the simulated cases were chosen by hand.
agent_relevance: Founding model for 'selection by code': one program settles which hypothesis set wins.

source: Holyoak & Simon (1999) Bidirectional reasoning in decision making by constraint satisfaction, J. Exp. Psychol.: General 128(1):3-31
finding: From memory, not opened: people given a legal case rated evidence and the verdict before and after; ratings of evidence moved toward the verdict they ended up choosing (coherence shift), as a constraint-satisfaction network predicts, and not as a one-way rational model predicts.
numbers: Not verified this session: effect sizes and N need to be read from the paper.
limits: Student participants, short vignette cases. Network fits were qualitative.
agent_relevance: Gives the human baseline for distortion: an agent that scores evidence after it has a leaning verdict will inflate support. Score evidence before the verdict, by code.

source: Simon, Pham, Le, Holyoak (2001) The emergence of coherence over the course of decision making, J. Exp. Psychol.: Learning, Memory, and Cognition 27(5):1250-1260
finding: From memory, not opened: coherence between evidence and choice builds up during deliberation and is not present at the start. Preferences are constructed.
numbers: Not verified this session.
limits: Not read.
agent_relevance: Coherence in the final state is not evidence that it was there in the inputs.

source: Simon, Snow, Read (2004) The redux of cognitive consistency theories: Evidence judgments by constraint satisfaction, J. Personality and Social Psychology 86(6):814-837
finding: From memory, not opened: several experiments on a legal-style case in which the strength of arguments or evidence was rated before and after the verdict; ratings shifted toward the chosen side, and the shift persisted. Presented as a modern revival of cognitive consistency theory.
numbers: Not verified this session.
limits: Not read. Check whether reported shifts survive when the pre-rating is taken far from the decision.
agent_relevance: Same as b13.

source: Simon, Stenstrom, Read (2015) The coherence effect: Blending cold and hot cognitions, J. Personality and Social Psychology
finding: From memory, not opened: coherence shifts also occur when the case contains emotional elements; a later extension of the constraint-satisfaction account.
numbers: Not verified this session.
limits: Not read.
agent_relevance: Moderator to check: emotion in the input may increase distortion; for an agent, strip affect-laden framing before scoring.

source: Glockner (2007) and Glockner & Engel (2013) parallel constraint satisfaction models of legal and juror judgment
finding: From memory, not opened: Glockner and colleagues test a parallel constraint satisfaction model (PCS) of intuitive judgment with legal cases, including mock jurors, with predictions on confidence and decision time that a purely rule-based account does not make.
numbers: Not verified this session.
limits: Not read; details of samples and effect sizes unknown here.
agent_relevance: A rival way to test networks: use confidence and time as signals, not only final verdicts.

source: Russo, Medvec, Meloy (1996) The distortion of information during decisions; Russo et al. (2008) goal of consistency as a cause of information distortion
finding: From memory, not opened: an independent line of work on 'predecisional distortion': people rate new information as supporting the currently leading option, which then pushes the leader further ahead. It occurs in consumer, auditing, and legal-like choices and is explained by a drive for consistency, not by a network model.
numbers: Not verified this session.
limits: Not read. A rival explanation of the same behaviour; network models and consistency-drive accounts are hard to tell apart on verdicts alone.
agent_relevance: Convergent evidence that the distortion is real, whatever the mechanism. Supports forcing a rating of each item before any leader is known.

source: Araszkiewicz (2013) Limits of constraint satisfaction theory of coherence as a theory of (legal) reasoning, in Coherence: Insights from Philosophy, Jurisprudence and AI, Springer
finding: Only the record page was opened (no abstract, no full text, no access). Title and venue confirmed: a critique of the constraint satisfaction theory of coherence as a theory of legal reasoning.
numbers: None.
limits: Content not read. Do not cite its claims until the text is read.
agent_relevance: Pointer to the main legal-theory critique; read before claiming the model is adequate for law.

source: Rival: Bayesian and probabilistic accounts of coherence (Bovens & Hartmann 2003; Olsson 2005 Against Coherence; Harris & Hahn 2009)
finding: From memory, not opened: probabilistic work argues that coherence is not truth-conducive in general and that no single coherence measure exists that always tracks truth. Experiments on multiple testimonies show people treat agreement among sources as extra evidence, but a Bayesian model with source reliability explains this without a coherence network.
numbers: Not verified this session.
limits: Not read.
agent_relevance: Why selection by coherence alone is risky: pair it with a reliability weight on each source and with held-out checks (guardrail G3).

source: Cross-study synthesis (b01, b03, b05): constraint solvers on top of LLM claims
finding: Three independent 2021-2022 systems give a consistent picture: a MaxSAT or factor-graph step over the model's own claims lifts consistency by 10 to 25 points and accuracy by 2 to 17 points, with the largest gains where the constraints are exact and numerous, and smallest on open QA.
numbers: BeliefBank +17 points accuracy (Macaw, simple facts); ConCoRD +5 points on ConVQA LXMERT, +1.4 to +1.9 F1 on NQ; Maieutic +11 points over self-consistency on Com2Sense dev.
limits: Different base models, benchmarks, and constraint sources, so sizes are not comparable. All pre-2023 models; no tests found this session on frontier models.
agent_relevance: Use the solver where constraints are exact (lists of claims with known logical relations). On open tasks expect little.

source: Cross-study synthesis: where the link weights come from
finding: In every LLM system above, results depend on how the links were produced: hand-made gold constraints (BeliefBank), NLI model (ConCoRD, Maieutic), self-query (Entailer). Gold constraints give the highest gains; NLI-detected links give less.
numbers: ConCoRD oracle vs ConCoRD NQ T5-3B: 0.423 vs 0.351. Maieutic: replacing NLI with likelihood links loses about 7%.
limits: Across-paper comparison.
agent_relevance: The weak point of ECHO-style selection is the same as in 1989: someone has to supply the links. Code should check that links come from checkable relations.

source: Cross-study synthesis: gaps in the record for LLMs and coherence shift
finding: I could not find, in the limited access this session, any LLM study that measures coherence shift (rating evidence after a verdict) the way Holyoak and Simon did, nor a direct ECHO-vs-LLM test. arXiv search was rate limited (HTTP 429) and the search budget was used up. This is a coverage gap, not evidence that none exists.
numbers: None.
limits: Absence of results here is not absence of studies. Check Semantic Scholar and arXiv again.
agent_relevance: Open question worth a direct test with our own harness: does an LLM that is asked to judge evidence after it commits show human-like shifts, and does separating the rating step remove it?

source: BeliefBank limits as a rival-explanation check
finding: The constraint solver can reduce accuracy when many weak, partly wrong constraints stack up against a strong correct belief. This is the machine version of coherence pulling a true claim toward a false but well-connected story.
numbers: Example: raw model right that a rat is not a cat; the solver flips it because several weak constraints (catches mice, has tail) outweigh the strong 'rat is not a feline' constraint. Constraint weights tuned by grid search on 1,072 dev facts.
limits: Anecdotal error analysis, no rate given in what I read.
agent_relevance: Cap the influence of weak links; give hard constraints (known logical facts) infinite weight; log every flip so it can be audited.

source: Entailer, rival explanation: belief errors dominate failures
finding: Even when a chain is faithful and checked against the model's own beliefs, a third of failures come from the model holding a wrong belief. Coherence with one's own beliefs cannot fix wrong beliefs.
numbers: Belief errors 33%, basic reasoning errors 10%, incorrect abductive inferences 9% of failures (Fig. 7). Zero-shot GPT-3 OBQA 57.6 and few-shot 65.4 quoted as context; PaLM-540B with rationale ensembling 91.0.
limits: 11B model, science QA.
agent_relevance: Pair coherence selection with grounded checks (G2, G3). Self-agreement is a hint, not proof.

source: IBE-Eval human comparison: LLM judge vs coded features
finding: A GPT-3.5 judge correlates weakly with human preference on which explanation is more plausible; a small linear model over counted features correlates more strongly.
numbers: Spearman 0.31 (n.s.) for GPT-3.5 judge vs 0.64 (p<.01) for IBE-Eval, on 100 explanation pairs; two raters, kappa .68.
limits: Small sample, raters were authors, GPT-3.5 is an old judge by 2026.
agent_relevance: Supports counting features by code over asking the model to judge, in line with the schema's rule that judged steps add noise.
